title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 44 (Nature of Shares or Debentures)

content.overview: Section 44 provides that the shares, debentures or other interest of any member in a company shall be movable property transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company.
content.glance: Shares, debentures and member interests are movable property; transferability follows the articles and the statutory transfer framework.
content.study: The shares or debentures or other interest of any member in a company are movable property transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company. The section establishes legal character (movable property) and points transfer procedure to the articles, read with the Act’s transfer provisions. It does not erase valid statutory, contractual or articles-based restrictions on transfer. Current-law framing: identify the interest; treat it as movable property; apply articles and statutory transfer rules for effectiveness against the company.

sections.heading: Movable Property
sections.body: Shares, debentures and other member interests are movable property.

sections.heading: Transferability
sections.body: Transfer is in the manner provided by the company’s articles, subject to the Act.

sections.heading: Restrictions Survive
sections.body: Valid statutory, contractual or articles-based restrictions on transfer are not erased by the movable-property characterisation.

examples.title: Share as movable property
examples.body: A member’s share is movable property, but the company may require compliance with the transfer procedure under the articles and the Act before recognising the transferee.

examples.title: Debenture
examples.body: A debenture falls within s. 44’s movable-property treatment.

hypotheticals.question: Does calling shares movable property make every transfer automatically effective against the company?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 44 characterises the property; transferability still follows the articles and the statutory transfer framework.

misconceptions.correction: Section 44 links transfer to the manner provided by the articles; statutory transfer rules still apply.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. It characterises shares, debentures and member interests as movable property; transferability still follows the articles and the statutory transfer framework.
